text.title: RSpec Testing for Rails Applications — Worked Example
text.summary: One end-to-end worked example illustrating the full procedure for `ruby-rspec-testing` against a representative task.

section.title: Scenario
section.p: Adding RSpec to a Rails service that creates a `User` and enqueues a welcome email. Owner: tl:alex; reviewer: tl:bob; cadence: per-release.

list.item: Each prerequisite supplied per the AGENTS.md table; sources linked.
Existing artefact catalogue checked for duplicates (none found).

section.title: Walkthrough
section.p: The team runs the five-step procedure in `content/04-procedure.xml`, recording one paragraph per step. At step 4 the self-check triggers a fix on the rationale (no input cited); re-check passes. The artefact emits with status='ready-for-owner-review'.

section.title: Second worked example — PlaceOrderService (isolated) + Orders request spec (full stack)
section.p: Rails 7 + RSpec + factory_bot. `PlaceOrderService` takes user + gateway + inventory + mailer; `OrdersController#create` delegates to it.

list.item: Step 2 — the service spec is `describe PlaceOrderService` with three contexts: inventory sufficient, inventory insufficient, payment declined.
Step 3 — the service spec uses `build_stubbed` for user and order; the request spec uses `create` because it asserts on persisted state.
Step 4 — `shared_examples_for "auditable"` checks created_by + updated_by + the audit_log association, and is applied to Order, Customer and Refund.
Step 5 — `--profile 10` shows the request specs dominating; the service spec runs in 80ms.

section.p: Outcome: service spec 80ms, request spec 1.2s, whole suite 90s instead of 8 minutes after the `build_stubbed` audit. Full spec body in `templates/place_order_service_spec.rb`.

list.item: The decision tree in `content/06-decision-tree.xml` saved one round at step 1 by ruling out a duplicate artefact.
Without the self-check at step 4 the rationale would have shipped without input citations.
